text: Lesson 13 left one conflict openly unresolved on the page. Scoping is where that conflict actually gets decided — deliberately, in writing — along with everything else that is and isn't part of Phase 1.

The categorization conflict resolves into a two-layer model, not a win for any one system. One shared, corporate-level top category list sits above domain-specific subcategories each hospital system configures for itself. St. Catherine's keeps its full multi-tier detail as subcategories, so its reporting still works. Lakeshore keeps local governance over its own subcategory list. Prairie View gets a real structure instead of free text, without being forced into St. Catherine's full depth on day one. Nobody gets everything they originally asked for — and for a genuine three-way conflict, that's the honest, correct outcome.

On that foundation, Phase 1 is the unified Service Desk's core: incident and request management on one shared catalog front door, domain-scoped ticket queues so each system sees its own tickets while Meridian's executives see the rollup, basic reporting at both the domain and corporate level, and a sequenced training and go-live plan — one pilot system first, then the rest, not a single simultaneous cutover.

Three things are deliberately left out, each with a stated reason. HR service delivery and facilities management wait for their already-planned later phases, so this workstream doesn't repeat the all-at-once risk Lesson 12 scoped around. Advanced reporting waits because it needs real operational data from a live Service Desk to be designed well. And a chatbot front end waits because it's a new support surface on top of a platform that hasn't gone live anywhere yet. Against the board's eighteen-month window, this phase runs roughly four to five months, with each system's legacy process staying fully supported until its own go-live — the real, written answer to Prairie View's concern that this time has to be different.
With scope decided and documented, Chapter 5 turns this written plan into the actual catalog items and workflows — starting with Lesson 15, building the service workflows themselves.
